summary: The /invoices heading now reads "Invoices (5)" — the number of rows the table below it is showing.
Why: nothing on the page said how many invoices were listed, so a reader had to count the rows.
What someone would notice: the <h1> on /invoices carries a count in brackets. The export button is unchanged and still reads "Export 3 invoices as CSV".

blocks.caption: After: the heading reads "Invoices (5)", matching the five rows in the table. The export button still says 3 — it counts what gets exported, not what is listed.
Before: a bare "Invoices" heading, with no indication of how many rows follow.

focus.title: The count is derived from the array the table maps over, not recomputed
focus.detail: The heading uses `invoices.length` — the same array `<tbody>` maps over — so the heading and the rows are structurally unable to disagree. This is also what honours the request's "after any status filter": there is no status filter in the app today (filtering is open issue #27), but when one lands and narrows that array, the heading follows it with no further change here. No new `lib/` function was added: counting an array is not a domain rule, and fundamentals.md asks for one domain module rather than a second near-duplicate.

focus.title: The count is one template literal, deliberately — adjacent JSX children would emit comment markers
focus.detail:
`{`Invoices (${invoices.length})`}` renders as `

Invoices (5)

`. Written as adjacent children (`Invoices ({n})`) React 19's server renderer emits `

Invoices (5)

`, which is visible to anyone reading or scraping the HTML. The `Total sent:` line two elements below already carries a comment saying this; the heading follows the same pattern. Verified with `curl -s http://localhost:3000/invoices`: the literal string `Invoices (5)` is present with no markers.

focus.title: The export button's 3 is untouched and is meant to differ from the heading's 5
focus.detail: Two numbers now sit next to each other on the page and they are deliberately different: the heading counts the rows listed, the button counts the rows the CSV will contain (sent and paid only — a draft and a void were never sent to a customer). That is the one product rule this app exists to hold, so one of the new tests asserts the heading does not read `Invoices (3)` while the button still reads `Export 3 invoices as CSV`, to catch anyone later "fixing" the apparent inconsistency by wiring the heading to `exportableInvoices`.
